draft.text:
AG-UI and WebMCP keep showing up in the same conversations, so it's easy to assume they compete.
They don't. They point in opposite directions.

AG-UI is the wire between your agent and your UI.
Your app streams the agent's work (text, tool calls, and state) and renders it however you like.

WebMCP is a proposed browser API that lets your page offer tools to an agent you didn't build: the one in the browser, an extension, or whatever the user brings along.

For me, one question settles it: who owns the agent?

→ You own it: AG-UI.
→ The user brings it: WebMCP.
→ Both: write the tool once and offer it through both doors. The shapes are nearly identical.

One caveat: WebMCP is still a draft in the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group and an origin trial in Chrome. Feature-detect, and don't put it on a critical path yet.

I wrote up the full comparison, with code for both. The link is in the first comment.

Are you experimenting with WebMCP yet? I'd love to hear what you're exposing.
